_about: Master data. This file is DATA, not logic — it is the owner's to correct. Every salary, threshold, spell and rate lives here so the engine never has to change when one of them does. It follows the Karigar & Staff Combined Master Prompt §3.3.
_derivation: Salaries marked derived were computed as (stated hourly rate x threshold hours). They reproduce the stated rate exactly; they were not guessed. rohanchavda's and varunkotecha's salaries were stated directly.
_threshold_hours_are_legacy: §3.6.3 calls Threshold Hrs/Mo a legacy reference column. Nothing prices off it: the daily rate is salary / threshold DAYS, and the hourly rate for the Work Report is the daily rate / the person's weekday shift (10 male, 8 female). The rows below are kept so the legacy column can still be printed.
_november_threshold: From 2025-11-01 devdave and rohanchavda move to 27 threshold days (26P + 2H) per §3.3.3. Everyone else stays on 28.
_provisional: The owner has now ruled on all seven FY2025-26 names. farhanamin, chetnavora, sanyabhatt, eshasolanki, aaravmehta and tanvigandhi have LEFT. kabirpatel is INACTIVE, not gone — the owner's words are 'we can associate in future' — so his spell is closed and his roster flag says Inactive, and a return is a new spell rather than a re-onboarding. None of the seven was given a leaving DATE, so each closes at 2026-03-31, the last date their own attendance data supports. That is a date the data supports, not a date the owner supplied.

meerachauhan is closed at the same date for the same reason. The owner confirmed FY2025-26 at 100 per hour, FY2026-27 on piece rate, that he is not employed as of now, and that he and ishitasompura 'can come to work as contract basis whenever I need'. So he is Inactive rather than left, and no FY2026-27 piece rate exists for him — a month that needs one raises.

devdave left in August 2026 and zarajoshi, aditivyas and darshdesai in July 2026. The owner gave months, not days, so each closes on the last day of the month named. Month precision, recorded as such.

rohanchavda's Flat flag is applied from his join date because §3.3.1 gives no start date and §3.4 asks for it to be confirmed. If it started later, his earlier months should scale with attendance instead.

The two piece-rate Dhaga-cutting hires §3.4 anticipated for Aug 2026 have arrived, so that PENDING note is retired. They are yashjadeja (piece rate, rate not stated) and nikhilthakkar (salaried at 10,000) — the source expected two piece-rate hires and got one of each, which is why the note is replaced rather than ticked off.

rohanchavda and hirenshah are both Flat: their pay does not move with a 28, 30 or 31 day month, or with a holiday taken. hirenshah's flag runs from his join date because the owner stated it in the present tense and gave no earlier boundary.

people._note: A trial. No employment spell on purpose — that absence is the point.

_rate_sources._about: Every piece_rate row above is cited here, against the source that states it. The self-test refuses a row with no citation, and refuses a citation that does not contain the rate it is meant to support — so raising 100 to 120 without re-reading the source fails a test rather than reaching a payslip. Piece-rate people with no row are listed in _no_rate_stated below.
_rate_sources.meerachauhan: 100 per hour. Stated four times and never contradicted: the §3.3 rate table row ‘meerachauhan | hours × ₹100 | 3.3’; the §3.3 locked formula ‘meerachauhan wage = Staff Report hours × Rs 100/hr (no monthly salary, no attendance tracking)’; the Part IV sheet formula ‘# meerachauhan wage = total meerachauhan hours × 100’; and the acceptance checklist item ‘meerachauhan wages = hours × Rs 100/hr (no attendance row)’. The owner later closed that period himself: "in fy2025-26 it was 100 per hour, in fy2026-27 it's piece rate", so the row now ends 2026-03-31 rather than running open into a year he described differently.
_rate_sources.ishitasompura: 100 per hour, FY2025-26 only. Stated by the owner in his own words: "meerachauhan/ishitasompura worked in fy2025-26 on 100/hour in FY2026-27 on piece rate so whenever I need they can come to work as contract basis" — one sentence covering both men and both years. The row is closed at 2026-03-31 because that sentence ends the hourly period; the FY2026-27 rate he refers to was never stated and is recorded in _rate_ends_and_no_successor_stated below.

_no_rate_stated._about: Piece-rate people the source names without ever stating a rate. They keep their pay_basis and deliberately have no piece_rate row, so a month that needs one reports Unresolvable instead of earning a guessed figure. This is not permission to pay zero — nothing posts.
_no_rate_stated.yashjadeja: Recorded by the owner as piece-rate for dhaga cutting, joining Aug 2026, with no rate stated. She is one of the two piece-rate dhaga-cutting hires the source anticipated in §3.4 and marked PENDING; the hire happened, the rate did not follow. Any month that needs it reports Unresolvable rather than paying a figure nobody set.

_shift_is_not_a_gender_rule: M and F above are shift GROUPS that happen to be named after a gender, not a rule about gender. Packing is the proof: bhavinraval and rhealakhani work 09:00-17:30 on a weekday and 09:00-13:00 on a Sunday, which is neither the male nor the female clock, so they carry shift_group Packing and their own two rows. A person's clock is a property of the person, and gender survives in this system only where the source says it belongs - the festival-leave rule. Adding a group is two rows here and no code change.
_weekly_off_is_not_a_company_rule: The owner: "2 Sunday every month as week off, only for rohanchavda and devdave, from Nov 2025 till present." Two people, not a policy — so it is a dated row against each of them, and nobody else acquires it by being male, by being a master, or by being senior. devdave's row is left open: what stops it applying to him is his employment ending on 2026-08-31, not a second date repeating that fact in a place it could later disagree with.
_weekly_off_did_not_compute_the_threshol: Both moved from a 280-hour month to 270 on the same date, and 280 - 2 x 5.0 — two Sundays at the male Sunday shift — is exactly 270. That agreement is CHECKED by test_weekly_off_agrees_with_threshold and is deliberately not a derivation. The threshold is a number the owner states; a system that recomputed it would silently restate somebody's closed month the next time the shift table was edited.
_leave_is_inside_employment: The owner: "nikhilthakkar on leave for a month". Leave sits inside an employment spell and never closes one — she has not left, and a month on leave is not a month she worked badly. Month precision, because a month is what was said.
_trial_has_no_employment_record: The owner: "Staff Trial: can be anyone who worked for few days or weeks and left and we paid" and "staff trail no joining no leaving, can come today and leave tomorrow if we didn't liked or negotiation failed". So this person has NO row in employment, NO salary, NO threshold and NO pay basis — none of those ever happened — and the payment below is the entire record. Named 'gauridoshi' rather than with a person's name because no real trial has been given to me, and inventing one would put a fabricated human being in a seed file.
_religion_decides_holidays_and_nothing_e: The owner: "RELIGION FOR HOLIDAY PURPOSE". So it is recorded, and gates.py has religion_only_decides_holidays() to keep it that way — the field may be read by the holiday path and by nothing that computes pay, hours, performance or permission. This is the same lesson as shift_group: an attribute that quietly acquires a second job is how somebody's wages end up depending on a field nobody thought was about wages.
_religion_is_recorded_only_where_it_was_: Only the people the owner actually named a religion for have one. The rest have NO religion field, and absence means NOT RECORDED — never a default and never a guess. A holiday that applies to one religion, matched against somebody whose religion nobody stated, raises and names them rather than silently including or excluding them from a paid day.
_meerachauhan_and_ishitasompura_are_two_: The owner: "meerachauhan/ishitasompura worked in fy2025-26 on 100/hour, in FY2026-27 on piece rate, so whenever I need they can come to work as contract basis." That is TWO periods, and the hourly row was left OPEN — so June 2026 resolved to 100 per hour, which is last year's rate paid into this year, and a note in this file claimed the opposite was happening. Both rows are now closed at the financial-year boundary. FY2026-27 has NO rate for either of them, which means a month that needs one raises and names the person: the owner has not stated a piece rate, and inventing one would be a wrong payment to a real person.

_rate_ends_and_no_successor_stated._about: A rate that RAN and then STOPPED, with nothing stated for the period after it. Deliberately not _no_rate_stated, which means a person who never had a rate at all — the self-test reads that field to check every rateless piece-rate person is explained, and folding a second meaning into it would make both readings wrong. Two facts, two fields. A month after the end date reports Unresolvable and names the person, exactly as a never-stated rate does.
_rate_ends_and_no_successor_stated.meerachauhan: 100 per hour ends 2026-03-31. The owner: "in fy2026-27 it's piece rate" — he named the basis for the new year and not the rate. Any FY2026-27 month raises.
_rate_ends_and_no_successor_stated.ishitasompura: The same sentence, the same date, the same consequence. "meerachauhan/ishitasompura worked in fy2025-26 on 100/hour in FY2026-27 on piece rate."
